plan: My private value is $13. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid close to my true value. Since the prize's value is randomly drawn between $0-$49, other bidders might have higher or lower values. I want to maximize potential profit by bidding strategically. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase my chances of winning, but not so high that I risk losing money if I win.

My value is $15. To maximize profit, I need to bid strategically. Since the prize is worth $15 to me, I want to win only if I can do so without paying more than my value. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase my chances of winning, but not so high that I risk a significant loss. A bid around $16-$17 seems reasonable - high enough to compete, but not so high that I'll lose money if I win.

My private value is $47, which means the item is worth $47 to me personally. To maximize profit, I want to win only if my net gain is positive. Since the second-highest bid determines my payment if I win, I'll bid strategically close to my value but not exactly at it. I'll bid $46.7 to leave a small profit margin. This approach balances winning probability with potential profit, accounting for potential competitor strategies.
